To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the solenodial dissipation rate of a compressible flow can be computed by using the incompressibie modeled dissipation-rate equations provided the additional term caused by variation in fluid viscosity is included.

the solenoidally filtered dissipation-rate equation of compressible flows is equivalent to that of the incompressible flows with an extra term that is proportional to the product of the solenoidal filtered dissipation rate, the dilatational filtered dissipation rate and the ratio of the dilatational to the solenoidal parts of the velocity gradient tensor.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for a compressible boundary layer, the solenoidal part of the turbulent dissipation rate is modeled in the same way as for incompressible boundary layers.
the incompressible κ-ε model is applicable to compressible flows, but the extra term due to the variation of fluid properties must be included.

the incompressible κ-e model is valid for the solenoidal part of the dissipation rate in compressible boundary-layer flows, provided that the extra term caused due to the variation of fluid density and viscosity is included.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the turbulent dissipation rate is modeled in terms solenoidal and the dilatational parts, the solenoidal part of the dissipation rate is calculated using the modeled dissipated equation for incompressable flows, and the dilatation part is calculated using the dilatation dissipation rate equation.

we have developed the theoretical foundation for using the κ-e model in compressible boundary-layer flows and we have also developed a rigorous basis for using κ-ω turbulence models in compressible boundary layer flows.
we have developed a turbulence model that is applicable to compressible flows and can be implemented in a general-purpose computational fluid dynamics (CFD) code.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the modeled equation for the solenoidal part of the turbulent dissipation rate is valid in a compressible turbulent boundary layer provided that the extra term due to the viscosity variation in the flow is included.

the solenoidality of turbulence is a key property that needs to be preserved when developing turbulence models for compressible flows, and that the dilatational dissipation rate should be modeled independently of the solenoidal part.
the incompressible κ-e equations can be applied to compressible flows provided the extra term due to viscosity variation is included.
